title: Home, mosque, Jummah and exemptions
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Spring 2: The Prophet ﷺ as leader; Shahadah and Salah (1.7, 3.1, 3.2)
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y10 lesson 24 (Pupil PDF worksheet: home, mosque, Jummah and exemptions)
intro: Lesson 24: 3.2 Salah at home, in the mosque and at Jummah (Qur'an 62:9-11); exemptions. To understand where Muslims pray, the importance of Jummah, and who is exempt from salah

questions.q: Explain what 62:9-11 teaches about Jummah and work. (4 marks, our own question)
questions.a: Muslims must leave trade at the call for Jummah because worship comes first, but may return to work afterwards, remembering Allah.
questions.model: Point 1: worship comes before business. Develop: 'leave trade. That is better for you' (62:9). Point 2: work is also good. Develop: 'disperse in the land and seek from the bounty of Allah' (62:10), so Islam balances worship and earning.

questions.q: Congregational prayer is ... times the reward.
Shortening prayers when travelling is in ...
In the portal response box: 'Explain how Islam makes salah possible for everyone.' Use three exemptions or concessions with evidence. Start: 'Islam never asks more than a person can bear, so ...'
questions.model: Teacher writes: 'Islam never asks more than a person can bear (2:286), so someone who is ill may pray sitting (Bukhari).'

questions.a: Adhan, khutbah in two parts, two rak'ahs led by the imam.

questions.q: how could a Muslim pupil in a UK school attend Jummah?
questions.a: Ask for a timetable adjustment or a prayer room; the Equality Act protects religious practice.

questions.q: Back to our ponder: big sale at 1 pm on Friday: what to do?
questions.a: Leave trade for Jummah (62:9), then return to seek Allah's bounty (62:10).
